convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:4: * Reusable, DB-free helpers for artifact name-search results.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:8: * Artifact names are NOT unique: the same name can occur on many artifacts with
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:9: * different geometry (e.g. on device, "Bluff Trail" x5, "9 Line Trail" x11, each
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:10: * a distinct geom_hash). A search result is therefore a *name-occurrence keyed by
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:11: * geom_hash*, not just a name. Rather than show the raw 64-char SHA-256 hash in a
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:12: * cramped list, we show a small per-name SEQUENCE NUMBER. The full geom_hash and
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:13: * id still travel on every row for the detail card / FIT.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:15: * This file is pure -- no DB handle, no Compose -- so the numbering transform can
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:16: * be reused anywhere name+geom_hash rows need stable display numbering: search
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:17: * results, a maintenance/list screen, the alias accordion, etc.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:20: * RULES BAKED INTO assignNameSequence() -- read before reusing or changing:
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:22: *  R1. SEQUENCE IS PER-NAME, NOT GLOBAL. Numbering restarts at 1 for each
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:23: *      distinct name. So two "Bluff Trail" rows are #1 and #2; an unrelated
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:24: *      "Aspen Trail" right after is #1 again -- not a continuation of the list.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:26: *  R2. ORDER WITHIN A NAME IS BY geom_hash (ascending, lexicographic). This is
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:27: *      what makes the number STABLE: a given geometry always sorts to the same
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:28: *      relative position among its same-name siblings, so its number does not
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:29: *      change between searches, app launches, or devices (the hash is content-
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:30: *      derived). The number is a stable proxy for the hash.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:32: *  R3. SELF-SORTING. The function sorts internally; callers may pass rows in any
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:33: *      order and still get correct, deterministic numbers. Sort key =
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:34: *      (name lower-cased, geom_hash). The lower-casing MUST match searchByName's
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:35: *      SQL `ORDER BY name COLLATE NOCASE, geom_hash` so on-device display order
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:36: *      and the numbering always agree. If you change one, change the other.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:39: *      is case-insensitive (R3) but a *group boundary* is an exact-string change.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:40: *      So "Foo" and "foo" -- if both existed -- sort adjacent yet number as two
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:41: *      separate groups (each starting at 1), which is correct: they are
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:42: *      genuinely different names.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:44: *  R5. NULL HANDLING. Null name -> "Not Named"; null geom_hash -> "" (an empty
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:45: *      hash sorts first within its name group); null type -> "". NOTE: the
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:46: *      search QUERY already excludes "Not Named"/blank names, so in the search
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:47: *      path these defaults rarely fire -- they exist so the util is safe for
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:48: *      OTHER callers that may pass unfiltered rows.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:50: *  R6. ROWS WITHOUT AN id ARE DROPPED. A result must be openable in the detail
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:51: *      card, which needs the id; an id-less row is unusable, so it is filtered
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:52: *      out rather than shown.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:54: *  R7. INPUT CONTRACT. Each input row is a Map<String,String?> carrying at least
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:55: *      the keys "id", "name", "geom_hash", "type" (exactly the keys produced by
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:56: *      SpatialDbManager.searchByName). Extra keys are ignored.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:59: * Rules baked into the QUERY (SpatialDbManager.searchByName) -- documented here
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:60: * for the full picture, but enforced there, not in this file:
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:61: *  Q1. NON-SPATIAL: searches the whole table, NOT the map viewport (unlike the
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:62: *      queryXByViewport family). A match can be far off-screen. FIT (later) is
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:63: *      the only bridge back to the bbox-scoped display.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:64: *  Q2. SUBSTRING match: `name LIKE '%term%'` (finds the term anywhere in a name).
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:65: *  Q3. EXCLUDES unnamed rows: name not null, not blank, and <> 'Not Named'.
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:66: *  Q4. CAPPED at `limit` (default 200). A caller can detect truncation by
convoy/ArtifactSearch.kt:67: *      comparing result size to the limit and prompt the user to refine.

convoy/ConvoyCorridorWorker.kt:26: *   ONLY. This worker never downloads from them - it re-derives the corridor

convoy/ConvoyCorridorWorker.kt:29: *   recovery path on a release build.

convoy/ConvoyCorridorWorker.kt:34: *   would RE-REQUEST every tile from Esri and only then discover it already
convoy/ConvoyCorridorWorker.kt:35: *   had them - full network cost paid twice, which is real money on per-tile

convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:14: * Removes downloaded map tiles inside a bounding box. This is the AREA
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:15: * DOWNLOAD worker with the direction reversed: same bbox, same tile
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:16: * derivation, same progress/notification/completion plumbing -- the only
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:17: * substitution is that a remote fetch + insertTile becomes a local DELETE.
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:20: *   launchWorker dispatches on downloadType. Delete never touches the
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:21: *   network, has different completion semantics, and runs in seconds rather
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:22: *   than hours -- threading a "mode" through the download worker would put
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:23: *   two opposite operations behind one set of branches.
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:25: * ⚠ LAYERS ARE SEPARATE STORES. ConvoyDownloadWorker writes with
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:26: *       sourceName = if (layerIndex == 0) slotName else layer.cacheDir
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:27: *   so SAT's base imagery lands in SAT.mbtiles and each overlay in its own
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:28: *   file. THIS WORKER USES THE IDENTICAL RULE. Deleting only `slotName`
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:29: *   would clear the base and leave transportation/places behind -- which
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:30: *   presents as "the delete did not work".
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:32: * ⚠ RANGE DELETE, NOT PER-TILE. A bbox is a contiguous rectangle in x/y at
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:34: *   enumerating every tile -- ~18 statements instead of ~50,000. The ranges
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:35: *   are derived by grouping ConvoyTileCalculator.calculateTiles(), the SAME
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:36: *   call the download uses, so "delete what I downloaded" is true by
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:37: *   construction rather than by two functions agreeing to stay in step.
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:39: * NOTE ON SPACE: deleting frees pages INSIDE the .mbtiles; the file keeps
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:40: * its size until a VACUUM. That is a separate explicit action -- VACUUM
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:41: * needs roughly the file's own size in free space, so it cannot be fired
convoy/ConvoyDeleteWorker.kt:42: * blindly at the end of every delete.

convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:553:    /** CORRIDORBATCH-2026-08-05: queue corridor downloads for MANY tracks across MANY slots.

convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:571:    /** CORRMIGRATE-2026-08-07H: write a COMPLETED row for a delete that ran

convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:380: * PHASE 1 implements this from THE LAST 2 COMPLETED DOWNLOADS (Fred's spec):
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:381: * once QueueEntry carries `completedAt` alongside its existing `createdAt`,
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:382: * each completed entry yields a real observed rate of
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:383: * downloadedTiles / (completedAt - createdAt). Averaging the last 2 smooths

convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:385: * memory), and does NOT jitter with connectivity the way instantaneous
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:386: * throughput sampling does - which matters on trails where the link drops.
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:388: * Until then this returns null so line 3 does not render. Do NOT substitute a
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:389: * live-rate estimate here: an unstable number is worse than none.
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:391: * RETURNS Pair(duration, completionStamp) - BOTH go on line 3, because they
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:392: * answer different questions. Duration ("how long do I wait?") is what you
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:393: * want for a short job; a completion stamp ("when will it be done?") is what
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:395: * standing in a parking lot. A corridor job at ~894,507 tiles can genuinely
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:400: * COMPLETION STAMP - reuse the existing `dateFmt` ("MMM d h:mm a"):
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:403: * ROUND LONG ESTIMATES. A two-sample rate cannot justify minute precision: if
convoy/ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:405: * the "~" prefix and round anything over ~8 hours to the nearest hour so it

convoy/ConvoySourceMigration.kt:25: * structure. begin() must therefore be called BEFORE updateSlotSource, or the
convoy/ConvoySourceMigration.kt:27: * device) become orphans that nothing knows to remove.
convoy/ConvoySourceMigration.kt:29: * A file with no completed_at is an interrupted migration. Resume is a
convoy/ConvoySourceMigration.kt:30: * deliberate prompt, never automatic: finishing means deleting GB of tiles,
convoy/ConvoySourceMigration.kt:31: * and the launch that discovers it may be at a trailhead.

convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:220:    /** Divide bounds into grid cells at roughly gridMiles resolution */
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:223:     * SEGMENTATION SPLITTER  (replaces fixed-12-mile gridCells)
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:225:     * Splits one drawn bbox into ceil(realTotal / 50_000) roughly-equal cells so
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:226:     * no single download job strands a queue slot. Each cell is a FULL z-stack
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:227:     * slice (z10..z18) of its geography -> every cell same shape of work ->
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:228:     * comparable -> they finish together in parallel slots = load balancing.
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:231:     * WHY sizeTiles is passed IN (not just quickEstimate here):
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:232:     *   quickEstimate(bbox).tileCount = ONE LAYER's geographic tiles.
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:233:     *   SAT actually pulls THREE layers (base + 2 overlays) over the SAME
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:234:     *   geography, each a separate download. So the REAL job volume for SAT is
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:235:     *   quickEstimate * 3 (~24,716 * 3 = ~74,148). enqueueArea already knows the
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:236:     *   per-slot layer count (slotLayers), so it passes the REAL total in as
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:237:     *   sizeTiles. Sizing off the bare 1-layer number under-segments (this was
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:238:     *   caught by the dry-run JSON on 2026-07-11: a 74K SAT area reported 24,716
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:239:     *   and split into 1 segment when it needed 2).
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:241:     * WHY overlap is TILE-WIDTHS and SEAM-ONLY (not a fixed degree amount):
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:242:     *   Overlap only exists to stop a boundary-straddling tile from falling into
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:244:     *   1 tile at z18 = 360 / 2^18 = 0.00137 deg. The original spec used 1/8 deg
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:245:     *   (0.125) = ~91 tiles/edge, which BALLOONED a 24K area to 155K (6x) in the
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:246:     *   dry-run. So: overlap = OVERLAP_TILES tile-widths (default 3 ~= 0.004 deg),
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:247:     *   applied ONLY when numSegments>1 (a single segment has no internal seam,
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:250:     * Returns the SAME [north,south,east,west] DoubleArray shape gridCells
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:251:     * returned, so the enqueue loop in enqueueArea is UNCHANGED.
convoy/ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:252:     * Logs every cell under "SEGMENT" (adb logcat -s SEGMENT) for visibility.

convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:34: * ═══ THE FOUR WRONG TURNS, and why the code looks like this ═══
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:36: * ⛔ 1. DISTANCE MUST NOT BE IN THE SCORE. The first search scored
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:37: *    `poiValue - miles * 0.06`, which is a CHEAPEST-PATH search wearing a POI
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:38: *    bonus. It returned 5 features on 69 miles and NO SPRINGS AT ALL though

convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:41: *    miles until the budget runs out. `scoreSet()` takes no distance argument

convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:44: * ⛔ 2. PENALISE, DO NOT FILTER. Generating thousands of candidates, ranking

convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:46: *    with a shared spine every candidate shares it. Navigation apps do the
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:47: *    opposite: find the best, PENALISE its edges, re-solve. The second route is
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:48: *    then the best route that AVOIDS the first. See `penalty` below.
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:51: *    before it found anything. Explore to the ceiling, score, then apply the
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:52: *    rider's band as a CUTOFF on the results.
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:54: * ⛔ 4. THE GREEDY RUNS TO THE CEILING. With one target distance every restart
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:55: *    produced the same length. ⭐ Each restart draws its OWN target from the
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:56: *    range, so the pool spans it.
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:58: * ⭐ AND A POSITIVE-SCORE FLOOR IS REQUIRED. The iterative penalty eventually
convoy/RouteExplorer.kt:59: * makes every scoring corridor too expensive and the search returns the best

convoy/TileCodec.kt:12: * 35-40% aggregate storage-reduction goal:
convoy/TileCodec.kt:13: *   - BASE   (satellite/topo imagery, no alpha) -> LOSSY   WebP q80

convoy/TileCodec.kt:23: * FAIL-SAFE: if decode or encode throws (odd bytes, OOM), we RETURN THE
convoy/TileCodec.kt:24: * ORIGINAL BYTES unchanged. A tile is never lost to a codec error — worst
convoy/TileCodec.kt:25: * case it stores uncompressed, which still renders.
